candidates.description: Introducing the Hema Studio located in Gangnam, Seoul for those who like K-pop. Hema Studio offers tools allowing foreign tourists to record their favorite K-pop songs and shoot music videos. reviews: The booking was pitched like a makeover event where you’ll feel like a k-pop star for a day. If that’s what you’re after, you’ll be disappointed: this is not Rupaul’s Drag Race. The studio is in a basement office in a residential building, with entrance from the car park. They accommodated us in a small office with a desk and paperwork scattered over it and some office furniture. It felt we were invading the space of the office workers working silently next door. They ask you to make decisions before the day and provide them with an idea about the look and vibe you are after. I generated an AI picture of what I had in mind and sent it to them some days earlier. The make-up artist arrived and started doing her job, in the office/waiting room. I was sitting on a broken office chair. It felt like it was the first time this was happening, as they had to arrange for an extension cord for the hair drier. There was no consultation on what I wanted, no communication at all as I don’t speak Korean. it was exclusively based on the picture I had sent. There was no mirror in the office so didn’t know what was happening. I looked like a zombie and I didn’t like it. She did exactly the same makeup on my friend, it took 20-25 minutes overall and we were left to wait 40 mins in the office with not even a glass of cheap champagne or some background music to cheer us up. The description of the event is misleading: there is no behind-the-scenes photo and video highlights, and no real “k-pop outfit”: we were given a sparkly jacket and that’s it, makeover done. There is no “1:1 vocal directing” either, however we were asked to answer technical questions such as “which key do you want to sing in”, as I’m male but chose a song by a female vocalist. I dunno, a lower key? G-minor key? I’m no musician, I still don’t know what they were after. The video consisted of lipsyncing to your own unedited, horrible vocals being filmed from 3 different angles, with the office workers in the next room hearing how bad you sound. No other creative input was provided. I paid for 2 people as a duet, double the price but you are not buying double their time, just an extra sparkly jacket. I spend a massive $1480 and I never felt so awkward, out of place, embarrassed and ugly in my own life. They injected no fun in any of the activities at all. At the time of writing this immediately after the event, I haven’t received the video/edited vocals yet as it takes 2 weeks, so I’m not commenting on that. But I bought this for a bit of a magic experience and I hated every minute of it.
It was such a great experience. I'll definitely come again!

candidates.description: The Heo Jun Museum commemorates the life and works of the renowned Joseon-era doctor and scholar, Heo Jun. candidates.description: Located in Myeongdong, in the heart of Seoul, the Seoul Central Post Office goes beyond the capabilities of a regular post office by offering simultaneous interpretation to suit international business clients at its Sky Hall, and also comfortable and efficient conference rooms and reception halls available for a wide variety of functions.
reviews: The staff helped me get stamps for international post cards, as well as some for collecting.
Super efficient service and friendly staff helping out on ground. Special credit to the staff name 신태훈, he helped me to retrieve a very important item in my posted parcel box , thank you so much!!

If you went crazy shopping in Seoul like we did and are panicking about luggage weight… READ THIS. We shipped back 22kg worth of clothes, Korean snacks, cosmetics, and even a cooking pan through Seoul Central Post Office and honestly it was one of the BEST decisions we made during the trip. The best part that almost nobody talks about is their optional packing service. The counter staff suggested it to us because we originally thought of buying two boxes and packing everything ourselves. Instead, this uncle there professionally packed EVERYTHING into one giant box for us so it became much more affordable. The packing service cost 30,000 won CASH ONLY and it included: - The giant box - Bubble wrap/paper wraps - All the tapes and protective wrapping materials - The uncle packing everything securely for you And honestly… he packed it SO well. We were genuinely impressed by how experienced and efficient he was. Everything was tightly packed, protected, and organised perfectly. We paid around 140,000 won for EMS shipping for 22kg to Singapore, so altogether with the packing service, it was about 170,000 won total to ship everything home. SO worth it compared to dragging 22kg worth of extra luggage through train stations, airport transfers, stairs, and onto the plane. If you only have a small amount of items and want to DIY, they do provide paper wrapping materials and lots of tape there. The boxes are charged separately though. You’ll need to: 1. Take a queue ticket to purchase the box 2. Pack everything yourself 3. Take another queue number to pay for shipping There’s also an aunty there who speaks English and helps guide foreigners around, including helping you choose the correct queue number, so don’t stress too much if it feels confusing at first. For anyone looking for it: The international postage/EMS section is located in the basement, all the way to the left corner. And in case the English-speaking aunty isn’t around: - Press LEFT for buying boxes - Press RIGHT for the queue ticket to pay for shipping Would 100% do this again instead of suffering at the airport with overweight luggage.

candidates.name: Hoehyeon Secondhand LP Arcade
candidates.description: Hoehyeon Secondhand LP Arcade has nestled in an underground shopping center in Hoehyeon-dong since 1980s, and mainly deals in LPs (long-playing records) which have been discontinued. After reorganization of the shopping center in 2003, the number of the LP stores dwindled to just a handful. However, since domestic production for LPs stopped in 2004, this arcade has become a popular place with LP enthusiasts. Hoehyeon Secondhand LP Arcade is situated in Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center in the basement of Shinsegae Department Store; stores in the arcade stock secondhand CDs as well as LPs. Outside the stores, boxes are stacked with what appears at a glance to be thousands of LPs and CDs. Many of the record jackets are well-thumbed, reminding us how much history the albums contain. Seeing the musician’s name on each record is like peeking at an old movie.
